A typical pattern, not a client story

This page describes how this kind of work usually goes. For real projects, see the case studies.

Use case: security awareness for a team or family

The situation

Someone in the group nearly fell for a fake invoice, a "your account is locked" text, or a call from "the bank." People want to be safer, but most training they've seen was either scary or boring.

How it usually goes

  1. A short conversation first about who's in the room, what devices and accounts matter most, and anything that has already happened.
  2. One session, about an hour, in plain language, built around real examples: phishing emails and texts, fake support calls, payment fraud, password reuse, and data brokers.
  3. Hands-on time. Everyone turns on two-step sign-in for their most important account and checks their recovery details, during the session.
  4. A one-page takeaway with what to do when something looks wrong and who to tell.

For companies heading into an audit, a separate SOC 2 readiness engagement maps controls, gathers evidence, and fixes the basics before the auditor arrives. The audit opinion itself comes from an independent auditor.

What people leave able to do

  • Spot the signs of a phishing message and check it a safe way
  • Use a password manager and two-step sign-in on what matters most
  • Recover an account, or know who to call
  • Report something suspicious without feeling foolish
